items.title: Sales API (DeveloperStore)
items.description: Complete CRUD API for sales records with quantity-based discounts, as defined in the README use case.

items.title: Discount policy matrix
items.description: Replace the hardcoded README discount rules with append-only, scoped, time-bound discount policies managed through /api/discount-policies, and price every sale item from the policy in effect at the sale date.

items.title: Sale lifecycle
items.description: Add the discount snapshots and the Open/Closed/Cancelled state rules to the sales persisted by FEAT-010 (spec 2).

items.title: Sale read model in MongoDB
items.description: GET /api/sales/{id} and GET /api/sales read from a MongoDB collection (developer_evaluation_read.sales) that SaleProjectionHandler keeps from the outbox events, ordered by the outbox Sequence sent as the Rebus header outbox-sequence, with a tombstone for SaleDeleted; Outbox:PollingInterval drops to 500 ms. PostgreSQL stays the only write store.

items.title: Sale events through a transactional outbox
items.description: Record SaleCreated, SaleModified, SaleCancelled, ItemCancelled, and SaleDeleted in an OutboxMessages table inside the sale write transaction; a background relay dispatches them in Sequence order through Rebus over a PostgreSQL transport, and a Rebus handler logs them. At-least-once delivery with the outbox row id as message id. Reopened and amended by the FEAT-006 spec (§10): Rebus uses the MongoDB transport wired by FEAT-006, and FEAT-004 runs after FEAT-006.

items.title: Sale drafts
items.description: Manage drafts separately from confirmed sales, moving them out of the transactional database under significant order growth; discounts are re-applied on confirmation (spec E1).

items.title: Asynchronous sale intake
items.description: POST /api/sales with Prefer: respond-async validates the request, generates the sale id, sends the CreateSaleCommand through Rebus over the MongoDB transport, and answers 202; a Rebus handler runs the command through MediatR, idempotent on the sale id. Includes separate compose volumes and a console load simulator comparing the synchronous and asynchronous modes.

items.title: Discount policy approval workflow
items.description: Add PendingApproval, Approved, and Rejected statuses to policies; the resolver considers only approved policies (spec E4).

items.title: Discount policy cache
items.description: Cache policies in IMemoryCache keyed by scope, invalidated on write, with cross-instance staleness bounded by a TTL (spec E6).

items.title: Partial invoicing per sale line
items.description: Allow several invoices per sale item with invoiced quantity locked; the discount impact (freeze the percentage or forbid reducing quantity) is still undecided (spec E7).

items.title: Registry CRUDs
items.description: CRUD APIs for customers, branches, products, and sales (sales as a plain registry without discount rules), following the Users template; implemented before FEAT-001.

items.title: List filtering and ordering
items.description: Add the general-api.md field filters, * wildcards, _min/_max ranges, and _order to the customer, branch, product, and sale list endpoints.

items.title: Customer document (CPF/CNPJ)
items.description: Add a required, unique Document field to customers that holds a CPF or a CNPJ. Masks ('.', '-', '/', spaces) are removed and letters are stored in upper case; the type comes from the length (11 = CPF, 14 = CNPJ). New CpfValidator and CnpjValidator classes check length, characters, repeated sequences, and check digits; the CNPJ validator also accepts the alphanumeric CNPJ issued since July 2026 (12 characters 0-9/A-Z, check digits over ASCII - 48). Exposed through the customer create, update, get, and list endpoints. The migration deletes all existing customers before adding the column. A duplicate Document throws DuplicateEntryException, which returns 409.

items.title: Explicit transactions for write commands
items.description: Every CRUD write must open and close an explicit transaction: a MediatR TransactionBehavior over an IUnitOfWork, applied to commands marked ITransactionalCommand. Until then each write relies on a single SaveChangesAsync (registry CRUDs D7).

items.title: Upgrade AutoMapper past the known vulnerability
items.description: The build reports NU1903: AutoMapper 13.0.1 has a known high-severity vulnerability (GHSA-rvv3-g6hj-g44x) in the Application and WebApi projects. Resolved by a NuGetAuditSuppress with justification in the Application project: no mapped type nests, and AutoMapper 15+ needs a license key.

items.title: Remove duplicate CreateUser request mapping
items.description: CreateUserRequest to CreateUserCommand is mapped both in WebApi/Mappings/CreateUserRequestProfile and in Features/Users/CreateUser/CreateUserProfile; AutoMapper silently keeps one of them.

items.title: Stable sale item order
items.description: SaleRepository.GetByIdAsync includes items without ordering, so GET returns sale lines in database order, which can differ from the POST response.

items.title: GetCurrentUserId parses a Guid user id as int
items.description: BaseController.GetCurrentUserId calls int.Parse on the NameIdentifier claim, which holds a Guid, so it throws on first use; there is no caller yet.

items.title: Invalid login returns 500
items.description: AuthenticateUserHandler throws UnauthorizedAccessException, which no middleware maps (also after TASK-007); expected 401.

items.title: Duplicate e-mail on user creation returns 500
items.description: CreateUserHandler throws InvalidOperationException for an existing e-mail, which no middleware maps; expected a 4xx response.

items.title: BaseController.Ok<T> wraps every Ok response twice
items.description: BaseController.Ok<T>(T) shadows ControllerBase.Ok(object), so Users GET/DELETE, Auth login, and OkPaginated return a doubly wrapped body; fixed in FEAT-010 by removing the method.

items.title: GET /api/users/{id} returns 500
items.description: UsersController maps GetUserResult to GetUserResponse, but no AutoMapper profile defines that map, so AutoMapperMappingException becomes a 500. The User to GetUserResult map also left Name empty, since the entity property is Username; fixed with it.

items.title: Login returns 500 because of missing mappings
items.description: AuthController maps AuthenticateUserRequest to AuthenticateUserCommand and AuthenticateUserResult to AuthenticateUserResponse, but no profile defines them; fixed in FEAT-010 so write endpoints can get a token.

items.title: Null sale item returns 500
items.description: A null element in items passes the sale validators (ChildRules skips nulls) and fails with NullReferenceException; expected 400. Add RuleForEach(Items).NotNull() and make the duplicate-id rule null-safe.

items.title: Huge _page overflows the list offset
items.description: (page - 1) * size overflows int for very large _page; Postgres rejects the negative OFFSET and the list returns 500 instead of an empty page.

items.title: Money values with more than two decimals are silently rounded
items.description: Unit price, amounts, and DiscountPercentage are not validated against numeric(18,2)/numeric(5,2): extra decimals are echoed in the response but stored rounded, tiny values fail CHECK constraints with 500, and huge values overflow. Add PrecisionScale rules.

items.title: POST /api/users echoes empty user fields
items.description: CreateUserResult has only Id, so the CreateUserResult to CreateUserResponse map leaves name, email, and phone empty and role and status at 0 in the 201 response, even though the user is stored with the values sent.

items.title: Unique product code
items.description: Add a required, unique Code to products: text up to 50 characters, trimmed and stored in upper case, so codes that differ only in case are the same code. Creating a product, or updating one to a code another product already uses, throws DuplicateEntryException, which returns 409. Exposed through the product create, update, get, and list endpoints. The migration deletes all existing products before adding the column.

items.title: Carts and checkout into sales
items.description: Add carts (ids aligned to Guid) and a checkout that turns a cart into a sale through the transactional outbox: synchronous checkout in one transaction first; asynchronous checkout (FEAT-006) and carts outside PostgreSQL deduplicate on a unique Sale.CartId.

items.title: Users.Email has no unique index
items.description: CreateUserHandler rejects a duplicate e-mail with a read-then-insert check, but the Users table has no unique index on Email, so two concurrent requests with the same e-mail can both store a user.

items.title: Sale events to the application log
items.description: After a sale write commits, the create, update, and delete sale handlers raise SaleCreated, SaleModified, SaleCancelled, and ItemCancelled, and an IEventPublisher writes them to the application log. No outbox and no message broker (README: events may simply be logged). Replaces the event part of the cancelled FEAT-004. Cancelled: the reopened FEAT-004 outbox covers the README events.

items.title: Outbox relay shutdown behavior
items.description: A graceful shutdown during a relay cycle re-sends one event: SendLocal completes, then SaveChangesAsync sees the cancelled stopping token and ProcessedAt is not saved (save it with CancellationToken.None after a successful publish). Shutdown can also wait up to the host timeout when MongoDB is unreachable, since IBus.SendLocal takes no cancellation token.

items.title: Value equality for SaleSnapshot items
items.description: SaleSnapshot is a record whose Items is an IReadOnlyList, so record equality compares the list by reference and two identical snapshots are unequal. Use a value-equality collection or document it before a consumer compares snapshots.

items.title: Inject IMessageContext in SaleEventLogHandler
items.description: SaleEventLogHandler reads the static MessageContext.Current for the message id; inject IMessageContext instead so the handler can be unit-tested. Absorbed by FEAT-003 (TASK-076): both handlers inject IMessageContext, and SaleEventLogHandlerTests exists.

items.title: Remove the unused UserRegisteredEvent
items.description: Domain/Events/UserRegisteredEvent.cs comes from the original template and nothing references it: no code raises, publishes, or handles it, and no test uses it. Delete the file.

items.title: User endpoints accept anonymous requests
items.description: UsersController has no [Authorize] attribute and the app sets no fallback authorization policy, so GET /api/users/{id} (confirmed: 200 without a token) and DELETE /api/users/{id} run without a token: anyone can read or delete any user. POST /api/users is the sign-up path used before any token exists, and the caller chooses the new user's role, Admin included; the fix must decide whether sign-up stays anonymous and which roles it may grant.

items.title: Trace console: keys no scenario exercises
items.description: The trace console's full run cannot exercise eight documented keys, which the summary lists as expected misses: SAL-CRT-06 (redelivered queued command), SAL-OBW-02 (outbox write outside a transaction), SAL-RLY-07 (failed relay cycle), SAL-DSP-07 (failed dispatch), SAL-BUS-06 (retried delivery; only fail-fast validation failures are provoked), USR-SED-06 (seed skip; the run always starts from a wiped database), CMN-RSP-10 (unhandled exception; no scenario provokes one), SAL-PRJ-02 (an event older than the read model document; only a redelivery, or two events of one sale in one relay batch, produces one). Covering them needs fault injection or a redelivery in a scenario.

items.title: Disable discount policies
items.description: Replaces the edit path: POST /api/discount-policies/disable (Admin, Manager) takes a list of policy ids and marks them with DisabledAt, all or nothing (an unknown id answers 404 and nothing is written); a disabled policy leaves the resolution (IsInEffectAt and GetApplicableAsync require DisabledAt null) while stored sale snapshots stay; GET by id and the list show disabledAt, and the list hides disabled policies unless includeDisabled=true. Not reversible: to bring a rule back, create a new policy. Spec amendment A24.

items.title: Audit columns on every PostgreSQL table

items.title: Request-validator 400 bodies use the raw FluentValidation array
items.description: Every controller (FEAT-010 and the discount policy feature) returns BadRequest(validationResult.Errors) from the request validators, a raw array, while handler-level rejections go through ValidationExceptionMiddleware as { success, message, errors[{ error, detail }] }. Unify on the middleware envelope for all controllers. Absorbed by FEAT-018: the 28 sites changed there.

items.title: SaleItems snapshot columns: drop the migration defaults and bound computed amounts
items.description: AddSaleItemDiscountSnapshot leaves DEFAULT '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' / DEFAULT 0 on DiscountPolicyId and DiscountCeilingPercentage, so a raw insert that omits them gets an empty policy id. The computed DiscountAmount/TotalAmount are no longer range-checked before PostgreSQL's numeric(18,2), so an extreme unit price ends in a 500. Drop the defaults (or add CHECK ("DiscountPolicyId" <> '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000')) and reject amounts above the column range as 400.

items.title: FEAT-001 review leftovers: tests and docs polish
items.description: A test pinning the tier OrderBy(MinQuantity) in DiscountPolicyProfile; a DiscountTier.FindSetViolation doc stating that per-range checks are the caller's; the invalid-set theory in DiscountTierTests asserting the violation message, not only NotBeNull; truncating client ValidFrom/ValidTo to microseconds in CreateDiscountPolicyHandler so the 201 body equals a later GET; a SaleResponseProfile test for discountPolicyId, discountCeilingPercentage, and requestedDiscountPercentage. Also: the XML summary of RequestedDiscountPercentage says "null when the ceiling was applied" where it means the client sent none. From the TD-032 review: two concurrent disables of the same policy can overwrite the first DisabledAt (a conditional ExecuteUpdate WHERE DisabledAt IS NULL or a concurrency token would keep the first instant); the includeDisabled parsing of the list action (garbage, repeated key, case) has no automated test; when a field filter and includeDisabled are both invalid only the parser failures are returned; the listing integration test sets DisabledAt before CreatedAt, a state the API cannot produce.

items.title: Repository layout at the root: src/, tests/, README.md
items.description: Moves the .NET solution out of backend/ to the repository root so the layout matches .doc/project-structure.md (src/, tests/, README.md at the root). The API documentation backend/docs becomes docs/; the local-only planning folder docs/ becomes docs-private/. The challenge statement README.md becomes CHALLENGE.md and the guide README_.md becomes README.md. Paths in code messages, scripts, the Makefile, the PR template, and the docs follow; docker-compose.yml pins the compose project name so the running stack and its volumes keep working.

items.title: Rich Sale aggregate: no public setters, discount rule check in the Domain
items.description: Sale and SaleItem get private setters, a Sale.Create factory fed by SaleLine records, ChangeCustomer, ChangeBranch, and SetCancelled for the PUT, and items created or changed only by Sale; SaleDiscountRules and SaleDiscountLine move unchanged to Domain/Services. HTTP contract, error codes, events, schema, and step keys unchanged. Closes evaluation gap N9 (row C2).

items.title: Empty Location header on 201 Created
items.description: The six create endpoints (users, customers, branches, products, discount policies, sales) answer Created(string.Empty, ...), so the 201 carries an empty Location header. They now answer CreatedAtAction pointing at the GET by id of the created resource, as the 202 of the queued sale already does with AcceptedAtAction.

items.title: Optimistic concurrency on sale updates
items.description: PUT /api/sales/{id} replaces the whole sale with no concurrency token, so two clients editing the same sale produce a silent lost update. Candidate design: PostgreSQL xmin as the EF concurrency token, exposed as ETag on GET, 201, and PUT (carried to the read model by the snapshot), optional If-Match on PUT answering 412 on mismatch and 409 on a race. Left out of the challenge scope by the owner on 2026-09-26 (evaluation gap N7).

items.title: Null check on Jwt:SecretKey in JwtTokenGenerator
items.description: JwtTokenGenerator passes _configuration["Jwt:SecretKey"] to Encoding.GetBytes without a null check, which the build reports as CS8604 (template code). A missing key now throws an InvalidOperationException that names the key, like the other required settings. Evaluation gap N12.

items.title: Bogus generators for Customer, Branch, Product, and Sale tests
items.description: Faker<T> appeared only in the three template User test files; the Customer, Branch, Product, and Sale tests built their data by hand. Adds Bogus generators in Unit Domain/Entities/TestData (a valid CPF for customers; SaleLine lines and Sale.Create for sales, since Sale has no public setter) and uses them in the entity tests. DiscountPolicy keeps its deterministic builder, whose tests pin the README tiers. Evaluation gap N1 (rows C12, T10).

items.title: Blind review: targeted fixes, scoped-policy guide step, and functional sales tests
items.description: Targeted fixes confirmed from an independent blind review of dev at 38abe5d. (1) Disabling a policy locks older sales for good (F04): GetApplicableAsync and DiscountPolicy.IsInEffect skip a disabled policy whatever the sale date, UpdateSaleHandler resolves at the stored sale date, and a new policy cannot start in the past, so after the default policy is disabled every PUT of an older sale, cancellation included, answers 400 NoDiscountPolicy with no way to repair it; keep a disabled policy in effect for sales dated before its DisabledAt, and update DSC-DIS-05. (2) Comments that point outside the repository (F11): about 13 comments cite spec anchors a reader cannot open (spec section 3.5, spec section 4, A2, A11, A14, A15, D9, D10) and about 10 name the README rules, tiers, or policy, which now live in CHALLENGE.md; state the rule itself and say challenge. (3) Error body deviation not stated (F06, docs only): docs/INDEX.md says CMN-RSP names where the body differs from .doc/general-api.md, but CMN-RSP only describes the implemented meaning; add the sentence (error carries the first failure code, detail a JSON array of messages, instead of human-readable summary and explanation). (4) Leftovers (F18): IJwtTokenGenerator registered twice in AddJwtAuthentication; BaseController.GetCurrentUserId and GetCurrentUserEmail have no caller and throw NullReferenceException; the root Dockerfile duplicates src/Ambev.DeveloperEvaluation.WebApi/Dockerfile, which compose uses (the root launchSettings.json, docker-compose.dcproj, and docker-compose.override.yml stay: they are the Visual Studio compose launch set). (5) DefaultConnection has no explicit check (F20): Program.cs passes it to UseNpgsql unchecked, so a missing key fails with an EF message that does not name it, unlike README section 7 promises; check it like the other settings. (6) Scoped policies are invisible in the guide: README section 5 only sells with the seeded default policy and calls it the README rule; add a step after step 4 that creates a policy for $PRODUCT with its own cap and tiers (validFrom a few seconds ahead, with the date command for macOS and Linux, since a policy cannot start in the past), sells that product under it, and states that a policy applies per product, per branch, both, or neither, resolved at the sale date by precedence (product and branch, product, branch, default); no seeded products or scoped policies, which would change the integration test counts and the trace and simulator results. (7) No automated test proves the challenge sales rules through HTTP (evaluation gap N2, blind review F14): the unit tests check the numbers with mocks and the trace console walks the paths without asserting values, outside CI. Add a class in tests/Ambev.DeveloperEvaluation.Functional that hosts the API with WebApplicationFactory against throwaway PostgreSQL and MongoDB databases (as PostgresFixture does), creates customer, branch, and product over HTTP under the seeded default policy, and asserts from the POST and PUT response bodies (not GET, which reads the eventually consistent read model): 3 units get no discount, 4 get 10%, 9 get 10%, 10 get 20%, 20 are allowed with 20%, 21 across lines answer 400 QuantityLimitExceeded, a requested discount above the ceiling answers 400 DiscountAboveAllowed, a discount with 3 units answers 400, item and sale totals, the unit price copied from the catalog, and cancelling one line reprices the others. Left out by design: F05 (the challenge rules are the seeded default policy; scoped policies may set their own cap and tiers on purpose, FEAT-001). Confirmed and left out: F12 (the DELETE in AddProductCode and AddCustomerDocument is a no-op on a new database and the migrations are already released), F06 contract change, F15, F16, F19, and the design findings F02 and F03.
